# lowob

> Commercial growth for complex markets: strategy, growth, distribution and revenue.

## Core pages

- [Operator experience. Studio flexibility.](https://www.lowob.com/about/): Senior commercial judgment and studio flexibility for complex markets.
- [Tell us where the business is getting stuck.](https://www.lowob.com/contact/): Tell lowob where the business is getting stuck and send a focused commercial brief.
- [Distribution](https://www.lowob.com/distribution/): Distribution services from lowob: Put real distribution behind the strategy.
- [Growth](https://www.lowob.com/growth/): Growth services from lowob: Turn the strategy into activity people can see, understand, and act on.
- [Commercial growth for complex markets](https://www.lowob.com/): lowob connects strategy, growth, distribution, partnerships and revenue to help companies build commercial traction in AI, Web3, fintech, media and technology.
- [Privacy policy](https://www.lowob.com/privacy/): What we collect when you send a brief or read the site; why; who sees it; and how to ask us to stop.
- [Useful expertise. Not a content mill.](https://www.lowob.com/research/): Practical Lowob research across strategy, growth, distribution, and revenue in complex markets.
- [Revenue](https://www.lowob.com/revenue/): Revenue services from lowob: Convert market activity into commercial traction.
- [Strategy](https://www.lowob.com/strategy/): Strategy services from lowob: Understand the market before trying to scale into it.
- [Terms of use](https://www.lowob.com/terms/): The terms for reading lowob.com and its Research. Client engagements run on a written scope, which takes precedence over anything here.

## Research

- ["40,000 members and nobody does anything"](https://www.lowob.com/research/40-000-members-and-nobody-does-anything/): A large, silent community was recruited for a payout and never given a job.
- [A loop with good context](https://www.lowob.com/research/a-loop-with-good-context/): An agent is a loop, and the context it most needs is prior judgment on comparable cases. How to add a precedent slot, and how to test it blind.
- [A reviewer who does not verify is not a control](https://www.lowob.com/research/a-reviewer-who-does-not-verify-is-not-a-control/): Human-in-the-loop is a design pattern, not a defence. Courts, regulators and clients now look for evidence that the human actually checked.
- [Ad Network vs Ad Exchange vs DSP: The Middlemen](https://www.lowob.com/research/ad-network-vs-exchange-vs-dsp/): Ad networks, ad exchanges, and DSPs all sit between your budget and a publisher. What each does, how each is paid, and which one you are actually dealing with.
- [Your Affiliate Program Is Either an Asset You Own or a Coupon Leak You Pay For.](https://www.lowob.com/research/affiliate-program-asset-or-coupon-leak/): Playbook from lowob Research: Your Affiliate Program Is Either an Asset You Own or a Coupon Leak You Pay For.
- [Affiliate vs Partner vs Referral Programs: The Difference](https://www.lowob.com/research/affiliate-vs-partner-vs-referral/): Affiliate, partner and referral programs all pay third parties to bring customers. How each works, who runs it, and which one a company needs.
- [Agency Types Explained: Full-Service to Specialist](https://www.lowob.com/research/agency-types-field-guide/): Not all agencies do the same work. A field guide to the main types, what each is good at, how each is paid, and the questions that reveal which one you need.
- [Agency vs Consultancy vs Advisor vs Fractional: Explained](https://www.lowob.com/research/agency-vs-consultancy-vs-advisor/): What an agency, a consultancy, an advisor and a fractional executive each sell, how each is paid, and which problem each one fits.

- [An audience is not a business](https://www.lowob.com/research/an-audience-is-not-a-business/): An audience is an asset, not a business. A media business starts when you can say who the audience is, who pays for access to it, and which part you own.
- [Approval rate measures fatigue too](https://www.lowob.com/research/approval-rate-measures-fatigue-too/): "Accepted without edit" rises when an AI system improves. It also rises when reviewers get tired, trust fluency, stop seeing hard cases, or ask for less.
- [Ask for the gap, not the summary](https://www.lowob.com/research/ask-for-the-gap-not-the-summary/): A good judgment system doesn't ask people to tell it everything. It knows what the next decision needs, spots what's missing, and asks one specific question.

- [Below the volume floor](https://www.lowob.com/research/below-the-volume-floor/): At 150 decisions a year, all different, no model will learn your judgment, and pooling across companies does not rescue it.
- [Brand Safety vs Brand Suitability: What They Cost You](https://www.lowob.com/research/brand-safety-and-suitability/): Brand safety avoids harm; brand suitability judges fit. How verification enforces both, what over-blocking costs, and how to set standards that protect reach.
- [Brand vs Performance Marketing: Different Time Horizons](https://www.lowob.com/research/brand-vs-performance-marketing/): Brand versus performance is mostly a misunderstanding. What each does, over what time, how they interact, and how a small company should split its budget.

- [Calibration is the honest learning signal](https://www.lowob.com/research/calibration-is-the-honest-learning-signal/): A system cannot claim to learn by grading its own outputs. It can by comparing human predictions with outcomes it did not produce.

- [The first hundred](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-first-hundred/): The first hundred community members are recruited, not attracted. Hand-pick them, give them real influence and close the loop on every contribution.
- [The first two-fifths](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-first-two-fifths/): What has shipped as an "enterprise brain" is the context layer. It is the easy two-fifths of the idea, and it is the part being paid for.
- [The graveyard](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-graveyard/): The most valuable thing an organisation knows is what it tried and abandoned, and why. It is also the first thing lost when people move.
- [The humans carrying context are the price signal](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-humans-carrying-context-are-the-price-signal/): Forward-deployed engineer postings rose more than tenfold in a year. Enterprises are paying expensive people to carry the context their software cannot hold.
- [The model is not the product](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-model-is-not-the-product/): Buyers do not pay for a model. They pay for a finished job. Position on the job, prove every AI claim, and tell investors a different story from customers.
- [The Modular GTM Team: Why AI and Web3 Are Moving Beyond the Full-Service Agency](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-modular-gtm-team/): Operating Model from lowob Research: The Modular GTM Team: Why AI and Web3 Are Moving Beyond the Full-Service Agency
- [The people who vouch for you](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-people-who-vouch-for-you/): In fintech, community is the practitioners who advise your segment and customers willing to be named. Give them a job, pay openly, and measure referrals.
- [The pilot that survives security review](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-pilot-that-survives-security-review/): AI pilots die from security review, missing owners, demo-grade accuracy and pricing confusion. Design the pilot to pass all four before you sign it.
- [The reason nobody types](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-reason-nobody-types/): The operative reason for many decisions is political, personal, embarrassing or legally sensitive.
- ["The round has stalled"](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-round-has-stalled/): A stalled round is a process fault or an evidence gap, and the pass reasons tell you which.
- [The scale ladder](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-scale-ladder/): There is no single right enterprise brain. There is a right one for two people, a different one for fifty, and a very different one for 10,000.
- ["The story isn't landing"](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-story-isnt-landing/): When the story isn't landing, the deck is usually aimed at the wrong audience, built on a category word instead of a buyer, or hiding its evidence too late.
- [The trade must clear on the spot](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-trade-must-clear-on-the-spot/): People share what they know when they get something back in the same moment.
- [The transitions that break the brain](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-transitions-that-break-the-brain/): Organisations lose their reasoning at transitions: the first hire, an acquisition, a founder leaving, a platform migration. Each has a defence, cheapest before.
- [The user story before the token story](https://www.lowob.com/research/the-user-story-before-the-token-story/): Say what the protocol does for a user in one sentence with no token in it. Then give each audience one belief, and keep a claims register.
- [Thin Bidding: The Cheapest Attention Is Wherever Nobody Else Is Buying.](https://www.lowob.com/research/thin-bidding/): Analysis from lowob Research: Thin Bidding: The Cheapest Attention Is Wherever Nobody Else Is Buying.
- [Token or no token](https://www.lowob.com/research/token-or-no-token/): A token should reduce coordination cost or create ownership. If it does neither, don't issue one; if it does, the money you raise shapes your go-to-market.
- [Top 10 applied-AI events, Nov 2026–Jun 2027](https://www.lowob.com/research/top-10-applied-ai-events-nov-2026-jun-2027/): The vendor shows are where the roadmaps are announced. The analyst and finance-specific events are where peers in regulated firms compare what actually works.
- [Top 5 agent frameworks for production, by state model and cloud](https://www.lowob.com/research/top-5-agent-frameworks-for-production-by-state-model-and-cloud/): Framework choice in 2026 is mostly a cloud and vendor decision, not a technical one. All the serious options speak the same tool protocol.
- [Top 5 AI customer-service agents, by pricing model](https://www.lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-customer-service-agents-by-pricing-model/): Customer service is the one place outcome pricing has taken hold, because a resolved ticket can be counted.
- [Top 5 AI governance and audit-trail tools](https://www.lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-governance-and-audit-trail-tools/): Governance platforms became a real category in 2026: Gartner published its first Magic Quadrant for them in June.
- [Top 5 AI notetakers for decision capture](https://www.lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-notetakers-for-decision-capture/): Every notetaker transcribes well now. Five ranked on what matters for decisions: extracting what was decided and why, owning the record, and consent.
- [Top 5 LLM observability and evaluation platforms](https://www.lowob.com/research/top-5-llm-observability-and-evaluation-platforms/): This category consolidated hard in 2026. Three well-known names are gone or folded into bigger companies.
- [Top 5 tools for a founders' decision ledger](https://www.lowob.com/research/top-5-tools-for-a-founders-decision-ledger/): None of these is truly append-only. Every one lets someone edit an old entry.
- [Trust is the product](https://www.lowob.com/research/trust-is-the-product/): In fintech, trust is the product: borrowed from trusted institutions, proved in the order buyers check, with every money claim treated as compliance copy.
- [Two hundred people: reasoning that travels without its author](https://www.lowob.com/research/two-hundred-people-reasoning-that-travels-without-its-author/): At a few hundred people, founders make a small fraction of the decisions.
- [Two people: the founders' ledger](https://www.lowob.com/research/two-people-the-founders-ledger/): At two people, the enterprise brain is a single document and a weekly habit.
- ["We shipped everything and the number went down"](https://www.lowob.com/research/we-shipped-everything-and-the-number-went-down/): The product is proven and the number still fell, so the problem has moved to distribution; stop building, name one story, and work one channel.
- [Most KOL Campaigns Are Expensive Screenshots of Impressions.](https://www.lowob.com/research/web3-kol-campaign-measurement/): Analysis from lowob Research: Most KOL Campaigns Are Expensive Screenshots of Impressions.
- [Web3 Does Not Have One Customer. That Is Why Most Launch Plans Break.](https://www.lowob.com/research/web3-multi-audience-launch-plan/): Playbook from lowob Research: Web3 Does Not Have One Customer. That Is Why Most Launch Plans Break.
- [What an Advisor Does for an AI Company](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-advisors-do-ai-companies/): AI startups collect advisors quickly and use them poorly. What a good advisor adds at each stage, how to structure it, and the requests that waste them.
- [What an Advisor Does for a Web3 Company](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-advisors-do-web3-companies/): What a useful advisor does for a Web3 company today: distribution, sequencing, regulatory posture, and saying no to a launch nobody is ready for.
- [What investors fund in media now](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-investors-fund-in-media-now/): Investors fund media businesses with owned audiences that pay, proprietary products those audiences need, and revenue that does not depend on a platform.
- [What Is a Distribution Diagnostic? One Week, Explained](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-a-distribution-diagnostic/): A distribution diagnostic is a short, paid assessment of which channels can carry a product and at what cost. What it includes, produces and can't promise.
- [What Is a Marketing Funnel? And Why Full-Funnel Fails](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-a-marketing-funnel/): The funnel is the oldest model of how strangers become customers. What its stages mean, what it gets wrong, and why 'full-funnel' usually means no decision.
- [What Is a Press Release, and When Is It Worth It?](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-a-press-release/): What a press release should contain, how it is distributed, what it can and cannot do, and when it is a waste of money.
- [What Is a Restricted Category in Advertising?](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-a-restricted-category/): How ad platforms sort products into welcome, reviewed or refused categories, why legitimate companies get caught, and what it means for distribution.
- [What Is Account-Based Marketing? A Small-Team Version](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-account-based-marketing/): Account-based marketing concentrates effort on a named list of accounts. What it involves, when it is the right motion, and a version a small team can run.
- [What Is Ad Fraud? Bots, MFA Sites, and Controls](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-ad-fraud/): Ad fraud is fake activity sold as performance. The main forms, how it is detected, and the practical controls that keep a budget from paying for nobody.
- [What Is App Store Optimization? Fintech and Crypto Apps](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-app-store-optimization/): App store optimization is search ranking, listing conversion, and store review. Why fintech and crypto apps that cannot buy installs freely depend on it most.
- [What Is Connected TV Advertising? Should You Buy It?](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-connected-tv-advertising/): Connected TV is television bought like digital media. How it is bought and measured, what it costs, and when a mid-sized or restricted company should buy it.
- [What Is Conversion Rate Optimization, and When to Do It](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-conversion-rate-optimization/): Conversion rate optimization turns the same traffic into more customers. What it involves, what it needs to work, and when it is a distraction from traffic.
- [What Go-to-Market Means: A Plain Guide for Founders](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-gtm-for-founders/): A plain definition of go-to-market for technical and first-time founders: what GTM is and isn't, the four decisions inside it, and how to tell if you have one.
- [What Is Marketing Mix Modeling? A Small-Company Guide](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-marketing-mix-modeling/): Marketing mix modeling estimates each channel's contribution from aggregate data without tracking individuals. What it needs, and a version for small companies.
- [What Is Programmatic Advertising? A Plain-English Guide](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-programmatic-advertising/): Programmatic advertising is automated buying of ad space through real-time auctions. How it works, who takes a cut, and what the invoice terms mean.
- [What Is Retargeting, and Why It Overclaims Credit](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-retargeting/): Retargeting shows ads to people who already visited. How it works, why its reported results are almost always inflated, and how to run it without paying twice.
- [What Is UGC, and Why Brands Now Pay for It](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-is-ugc/): UGC now means genuine customer content and paid creator content styled to look organic. What each is, how it is used in ads, and the disclosure rules.
- [What Makes a Case Study Believable](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-makes-a-case-study-believable/): Case studies are evidence, not advertising. What a believable one contains, why most are not believed, and the version that works without naming the client.
- [What SEO Is Now: How Search Ranking Works Today](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-seo-is-now/): SEO has changed more in three years than in the previous ten. How ranking works today, what still matters, what stopped, and how AI answers change the job.
- [What Thought Leadership Actually Is](https://www.lowob.com/research/what-thought-leadership-actually-is/): Thought leadership is a defensible position with evidence and consequence. Why most of it is neither, how it differs from content marketing, how to make it.
- [Where judgment arrives first](https://www.lowob.com/research/where-judgment-arrives-first/): Judgment layers will work first where decisions are frequent, similar and graded quickly, and where someone will later have to defend them.
- [Whoever holds the record holds the company](https://www.lowob.com/research/whoever-holds-the-record-holds-the-company/): The layer that encodes how a business decides is the deepest lock-in in enterprise software. It is also where the strongest growth is.
- [You don't have three problems](https://www.lowob.com/research/you-dont-have-three-problems/): Fundraising, community and customer acquisition are three outputs of one commercial system.
- [Your first ten customers are design partners](https://www.lowob.com/research/your-first-ten-customers-are-design-partners/): Pick early customers for fit and learning, not logos. Agree a written success test, work closely for six to twelve weeks, then convert the ones that succeed.
- [Your first ten sponsors are design partners](https://www.lowob.com/research/your-first-ten-sponsors-are-design-partners/): Sponsorship, data and research are B2B sales. Treat the first ten buyers as design partners: agree the test and the report before money moves.
